text:
mike: Running into traces with no source/line info for our runtime when capturing with nsys inside our distroless-based perf image. kernels show as offsets (libruntime.so+0x1a2b3) and perfetto flame has anonymous frames. :(
jen: :eyes: Is this specific to nsys or also with nvprof/perf?
mike: Reproduces with nsys & nvprof capture; `perf record` shows symbols but no line numbers. `readelf --debug-dump=info` on the container binary shows no DWARF.
ruth: Are we stripping binaries in the container image? our build pipeline does a `strip --strip-debug` for smaller layers.
mike: Yes, the runtime debuginfo is stripped in the final image. But even when I mount the unstripped artifacts into the container, traces still don't resolve lines. Looks like CUPTI/nsys resolves names but can't map to source lines.
amara: Two things to check: (1) build-ids / debuglink matching between host debug files and container binary paths, (2) CUPTI version mismatch causing symbol collection to use host lib paths.
paul: Also check `-fdebug-prefix-map` — if build embeds original source paths that don't exist in container, the tracer may not find source files for line info. Could remap during build: `-fdebug-prefix-map=/home/runner=/src`
jen: Can you paste the `nm`/`readelf` output?
mike: snippet:```
$ readelf -S libruntime.so | grep debug
[NOBITS] .gnu_debugdata
$ file libruntime.so
libruntime.so: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, stripped
```
jen: Ok that explains missing DWARF. But you said mounting unstripped didn't help?
mike: Right. I mounted the artifact into `/opt/unstripped/libruntime.so` and pointed nsys `--symbols` but the flame still shows `libruntime.so(+0x1a2b3)`. `addr2line` on host maps the offset to correct file/line though.
ruth: Could be a build-id mismatch. `eu-readelf --notes libruntime.so` vs the mounted one to confirm build-id.
amara: Also check that nsys' capture uses libcupti from the same driver stack. If CUPTI in the container differs, it can record offsets that don't correspond. There's also known issue where nsys uses a bundled CUPTI which expects different symbolization paths.
paul: Another angle: containers with distroless lose `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id` layout. The kernel/perf tools expect `.build-id/xx/xxxxx.debug`. If those debug files aren't placed in that layout under `/usr/lib/debug`, `perf` can't auto-find them.
jen: For quick debug: run the container with the unstripped `.so` in place, and set `LD_PRELOAD` to point to it so the process actually loads that file path. If the running binary path differs from the symbol file path you'll still get mismatch.
mike: Tried `LD_PRELOAD=/opt/unstripped/libruntime.so` and `--capture-syscalls=true`; still mostly offsets. I can correlate addr2line externally but need nsys/perfetto to show lines for the trace.
amara: Try `--external-symbols=/opt/unstripped/libruntime.so` for nsys? IIRC there is a symbolization option to point to extra symbol files. Also `nsys profile --trace=cpu,cuda --output=trace` vs `nsys profile --sample=none` matters.
paul: And check `build-id` canonicalization: `objcopy --only-keep-debug libruntime.so libruntime.so.debug` then `objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink=libruntime.so.debug libruntime.so` and put `libruntime.so.debug` in `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/xx/` inside container. That tends to fix perf/addr2line lookup.
jen: If using CUPTI 12.x vs driver 11.x mismatch, nsys may fail at unwinding. What's the driver+cuda version in the container vs host?
mike: Host has driver 515.x, container had 525 toolkit. I also saw warnings from nsys about CUPTI registration during capture start.
jen: That mismatch could produce incorrect offsets in the CUPTI traces. Try using the same toolkit version in the capture environment as the host or use the nvidia-container-toolkit image matching driver.
amara: Also look at `--trace-children` and capture range. Sometimes we hit a scenario where the early JITed kernels produce unresolved frames because symbolization happens before modules are loaded. Use `nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx` and trigger capture after modules are up.
mike: Good call. I re-ran with capture starting after init and the number of anonymous frames dropped, but still a handful.
paul: If persistent, collect: `readelf -n libruntime.so` (build-id), `eu-readelf --debug-dump=info libruntime.so.debug`, `nsys profile --output=out --trace=cpu,cuda --sample=cpu` and attach the `.qdrep`. Infra can then try local symbolization.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: please attach sample qdrep and both stripped/unstripped libs. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/infra/nsys-symbols-debug
jen: One more gotcha — if the binary is loaded at a different base address (ASLR), perf toolchain needs the exact mapping from the trace. nsys writes module load events but if those are filtered out by container ioctl issues, symbolizer loses mapping. Inspect the qdrep for module events.
mike: I'll collect the artifacts and try the build-id objcopy flow. Thanks for the pointers. I'll post the qdrep and a tiny repro image next. :+1:
jen: Thanks — once we have qdrep infra can run a symbolization pass and report back. :mag_right:
